title: A step forward in Jamia, a long road ahead
where: The Editorial Page, page 12 (Editorial); report on page 4
syllabus: GS2 › Issues relating to education; Democratic participation · GS1 › Youth and society · GS4 › Trust, dialogue and leadership
summary: After an 18-day protest, Jamia Millia Islamia agreed to restore student union elections, dissolved since 2006, within a fixed timeline.
ideas: A guideline turned into a ban: the Lyngdoh Committee (2005) wanted to curb money, muscle power and outside political influence in campus polls; universities used it to scrap elections altogether.
Reforms meant to clean up student politics have often been used to suspend it.
Campus democracy is a school of citizenship: elections open campus decisions to students and give their grievances a channel; their absence infantilises young adults.
Student union elections train young adults in representative democracy and grievance redress.
Trust, not restriction: disciplinary action and curbs on essential services deepened the breakdown of trust; resolution came only through talks and a fixed timeline.
Fixed timelines and dialogue resolve campus disputes better than punitive discipline.
A wider pattern: Karnataka has approved student polls, Madhya Pradesh saw judicial intervention, Maharashtra set up a committee and Odisha is holding talks.
Several states are reviving student elections, showing a shift towards participatory campuses.
Youth demands for accountability: the protest echoed the movement at Aligarh Muslim University and the wider Gen Z protests seeking a say in decisions.
Campus movements reflect a wider youth demand for voice and accountability.
keywords: Guidelines for transparent, accountable student elections
The Lyngdoh Committee sought cleaner campus polls, not their abolition.
Treating adult students as unfit to decide
Suspending student polls infantilises young adults instead of trusting them with responsibility.
Students sharing in decisions that affect them
Participatory campus governance builds ownership and reduces conflict.
Time-bound commitments create graduated trust between administrations and students.
examples: Elections to be held about six weeks after 16 July 2027; disciplinary cases withdrawn
Jamia's dispute ended only when the administration offered a fixed timeline, showing that credibility needs dates.
Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha moving towards campus elections
Several states reviving student polls shows campus democracy returning to the policy agenda.
pyqs: Globalisation's impact on Indian youth, including the political sphere.
Autonomy for premier institutions: governance inside universities.
potential: "Student union elections are a nursery of democratic citizenship." Examine the case for and against their revival in Indian universities. (10 marks)
